Name: Harriett's Bookshop
Description: Named for Harriet Tubman, this Fishtown shop amplifies women, gender-expansive authors, and voices of color. Founded by Jeannine Cook — curated picks, author events, and a warm community spirit.

Name: Binding Agents
Description: Philly's only cookbook-focused bookstore, in the heart of the Italian Market. Deep selection of culinary titles from Philly chefs and beyond — food writing, memoirs, and technique. Opened 2024.

Name: Molly's Books & Records
Description: South Philly staple where you can buy, sell, and trade used books, records, and CDs. A digger's paradise — good finds, good prices, good vibes.

Name: A Novel Idea on Passyunk
Description: Part bookstore, part witch shop, part event space — a community-minded East Passyunk gem. Curated fiction, occult titles, local author events, and true neighborhood warmth.

Name: Wooden Shoe Books
Description: All-volunteer nonprofit infoshop on South Street since 1976. Anarchist theory, labor history, banned books, zines, and alternative press. One of Philly's most storied bookstores.

Name: Hakim's Bookstore & Gift Shop
Description: Philadelphia's oldest Black-owned bookstore, founded in 1959. A West Philly institution carrying Black history, Pan-Africanism, culture, and gift items. A true community anchor for over 65 years.

Name: House of Our Own
Description: A rambling Victorian house on the edge of Penn's campus filled with new and used books — scholarly titles, fiction, arts, and much more. Calm, browsable, beloved by students and neighbors.

Name: Uncle Bobbie's Coffee & Books
Description: Marc Lamont Hill's Germantown cultural hub. A Black-owned bookstore and coffee shop hosting readings with literary heavyweights. Strong in Black authors, politics, and fiction. A cornerstone since 2017.

Name: Giovanni's Room
Description: One of the oldest LGBTQ+ bookstores in the country, founded in 1973. Now run by Philly AIDS Thrift, it carries thousands of queer and feminist books, magazines, film, music, and apparel.
